column2: buildingSMART Deutschland awards the BIM Champions 2026
column3: On the eve of its Anwendertag, projects and people were awarded in three categories out of more than 30 entries; among the winners, a TU Dresden project on BIM in landscape architecture, integrated with GIS, weather simulations and AI.

column2: Portugal approves its national BIM strategy
column3: Council of Ministers Resolution no. 89/2026, published on 21 May, approves the National Strategy for BIM implementation on four pillars (public policy, standardisation, technology, training), with targets for public administration and the integration of BIM in procurement.

column2: EU BIM Task Group in Prague: data dictionaries and the new Czech law
column3: At the EU BIM Task Group workshop (28–29 April), public clients and European experts discussed legislation, training and data dictionaries; topics included the Czech law on information management in construction, published in 2025 and in force from 2027.

column2: buildingSMART International has a new Managing Director
column3: Aidan Mercer, at buildingSMART International since 2018, leads the organisation from 1 May 2026, tasked with implementing the 2026 plan and developing the openBIM brand.

column2: NRW: building permits on the BIM model
column3: Minister Ina Scharrenbach explains how North Rhine-Westphalia demonstrated with a study the feasibility of model-based building permits, and how to extend them to the whole state.

column2: Qatar: BIM and GIS for the national digital twin
column3: At Project Qatar 2026, the public works authority Ashghal shows how integrating BIM and GIS supports the national digital twin, from planning to infrastructure management.

column2: ASSORUP and ASSOBIM sign an agreement
column3: The association of Italian public project managers (RUP) and the BIM supply chain association will cooperate on training and initiatives for contracting authorities and professionals, to digitalise the award and management of public contracts.

column2: ISO 19650: the deepest revision of the series
column3: According to Volker Krieger of ISO TC59/SC13/WG13, the revision goes beyond the split between the project part and the asset management part and puts the whole life cycle at the centre.

column2: buildingSMART creates a «BIM and artificial intelligence» group
column3: On 6 July the board of buildingSMART Deutschland unanimously set up a working group on BIM and AI, starting from the open standards IFC, BCF, IDS and bSDD as the basis for using AI reliably.

column2: GeniusBIM: ASSOBIM's AI assistant on regulations and standards
column3: ASSOBIM launches a platform that answers in natural language on BIM regulations and standards, relying on an expert-validated knowledge base rather than a general-purpose chatbot.

column2: Singapore narrows the CORENET X mandate
column3: The BCA revises its plan: from 1 October 2026, submissions via CORENET X with IFC+SG models are mandatory only for new projects of 5,000 m² gross floor area and above; below that threshold they no longer are.

column2: IBIMI: three working groups on MEP systems in IFC
column3: In its Buildings domain, three groups start defining shared criteria for representing building services in the IFC standard, open to professionals, companies and software vendors.

column2: Basic BIM: guideline VDI/bS-MT 2552 Blatt 8.1 revised
column3: Six years on, the guideline on which more than 14,000 people in Germany were trained and certified has been updated; the draft remains open for public consultation until the end of September.

column2: UNI 11337-11: BIM enters permitting procedures
column3: The standard, published on 23 July, defines procedures and information flow for the e-Permit to authorise public and private works: model data also become a structured source for the authority reviewing the application.

column2: IFC 4.4 starts its path to an ISO standard
column3: buildingSMART International approved with 93% of votes (threshold 65%) the project to take IFC 4.4 to ISO, replacing ISO 16739-1:2024, which corresponds to IFC 4.3.

column2: Germany: the plan to make BIM mandatory in infrastructure
column3: Minister Alexander Dobrindt presents the «Stufenplan Digitales Planen und Bauen»: pilot projects, standards and common rules to reach mandatory BIM on large federal infrastructure projects from 2020.

column2: United Kingdom: BIM Level 2 mandate in force
column3: From 4 April 2016 all centrally procured public construction contracts must apply BIM Level 2, whatever their value. The BIM Task Group speaks of a result «unparalleled internationally».

column2: First parts of UNI 11337 published
column3: The UNI committee publishes parts 1, 4 and 5 of the standard on digital management of construction information processes: models and documents, levels of development of objects, information flows and requirements.

column2: Europe publishes the BIM handbook for the public sector
column3: The EU BIM Task Group, with public clients from 21 countries, presents the «Handbook for the Introduction of BIM by the European Public Sector», for a common approach to introducing BIM in procurement.

column2: BIM decree: Ministerial Decree 560/2017 signed
column3: Minister Delrio signs the decree that gradually introduces mandatory BIM methods in Italian public procurement, starting from 2019 for the largest and most complex works.

column2: UNI 11337-7: the BIM professional roles
column3: Part 7 of UNI 11337 is published, defining knowledge, skills and competences of BIM Manager, BIM Coordinator, BIM Specialist and CDE Manager according to the European Qualifications Framework.

column2: ISO 19650 arrives in Italian
column3: On 14 March 2019 UNI publishes UNI EN ISO 19650 parts 1 and 2, adopted by CEN in December 2018: the international standard on information management using BIM becomes an Italian standard.

column2: Brazil: committee for the national BIM strategy set up
column3: Decree 9.983/2019 establishes the Management Committee of the BIM BR Strategy, ahead of the BIM mandate for some public works from 2021 and its extensions up to 2028.

column2: UNI/PdR 78:2020: how BIM roles are certified
column3: UNI and Accredia publish the reference practice for the conformity assessment of the professional roles defined by UNI 11337-7.

column2: Brazil: BIM becomes mandatory in federal works
column3: Decree 10.306/2020 establishes the use of BIM in engineering works and services of the federal administration, with gradual introduction from 2021.

column2: Hong Kong: the first contract conditions for BIM
column3: The Hong Kong Institute of Surveyors publishes the «BIM Contract Conditions» with the BIM Contract Alliance, in response to the BIM mandate introduced by the government for public works.

column2: Ministerial Decree 312/2021: the BIM decree updated
column3: The new decree amends Ministerial Decree 560/2017: it introduces award points for the use of BIM in tenders funded by the Italian recovery plan (PNRR) and revises the deadlines, with the obligation only above €1 million.

column2: BIM masterplan for federal roads
column3: The Ministry of Transport presents the Masterplan BIM Bundesfernstraßen: by 2025 BIM is to become the standard for the technical management of federal motorways and roads, in three phases.

column2: South Korea: roadmap for the BIM mandate in public works
column3: With its smart construction plan, the Ministry sets the goal of digitalising the whole construction process by 2030, starting with the BIM mandate for public works from 100 billion won.

column2: IFC 4.3 approved as an ISO standard
column3: ISO approves IFC 4.3, which extends the open standard to linear infrastructure (roads, railways, bridges, ports and waterways) and becomes the new version of ISO 16739; publication follows in April 2024.

column2: Brazil: the new BIM BR Strategy
column3: President Lula signs the decree relaunching the national strategy to spread BIM, as part of the Nova Indústria Brasil plan.

column2: UK BIM Framework renewed
column3: nima and BSI update the free resource on standards and guidance for information management: content aligned with the ISO 19650 series, better navigation and an AI search function.

column2: Procurement corrective decree: BIM mandatory above €2 million from 2025
column3: Legislative Decree 209/2024 is published in the Official Gazette: from 1 January 2025 the digital information management obligation of art. 43 applies to new works and works on existing buildings above €2 million.

column2: La Spezia: the new roof of the Picco stadium born from a survey
column3: For the roof of the Curva Ferrovia stand, Exa Engineering starts from a point cloud and models the structure in Tekla Structures: all details for fabrication and erection come out of the BIM model.

column2: Camerino: former barracks become a cultural heritage hub
column3: For the Italian State Property Agency, the listed complex is converted with new steel structures; the project is managed in BIM, with documents coded according to the Method Statement and shared in the Agency's data environment.

column2: Nemetschek presents an AI assistant for Archicad at BAU
column3: At the BAU fair in Munich, the Nemetschek group shows its first assistant based on AI agents, designed for Archicad: it answers questions about the software and the BIM model and connects to visualisation. Launch is planned for the autumn.

column2: Hong Kong: BIM models become a binding part of tenders
column3: The Development Bureau updates the circular on BIM in public works, in force from 1 February: BIM remains mandatory above HK$30 million and, for tenders issued from 1 April 2025, design models are part of the tender documents and have contractual value.

column2: ISO 19650-6: safety information in BIM management
column3: The sixth part of the ISO 19650 series is published, dedicated to health and safety information: how to identify, share and deliver it collaboratively from design to operation and decommissioning. CEN adopts it as EN ISO 19650-6.

column2: Spain: public procurement with BIM exceeds 15 billion
column3: At the first «BIM en la contratación pública» day in Madrid, with about 300 professionals, the Ministry of Transport reviews the BIM Plan: public tenders requiring BIM exceed €15,000 million across infrastructure and buildings, led by the Community of Madrid.

column2: France: «BIM pour tous», BIM for small sites too
column3: The Fédération française du bâtiment launches the «BIM pour tous» call for projects: three pilot sites to show that BIM pays off in small operations too, both in design and in construction.

column2: Autodesk unifies design in Forma and announces «neural CAD»
column3: At Autodesk University in Nashville come Forma Building Design and Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs), with Revit as a connected client. Autodesk also announces «neural CAD» generative AI models, which in Forma should complete repetitive parts of the design on their own: for now these are announcements, not available products.

column2: openBIM Awards 2025 presented at the Berlin Summit
column3: At the buildingSMART International Summit in Berlin, with 765 participants from 49 countries, the openBIM projects of the year are awarded, chosen from 129 entries. Winners include Carleton University's open-source digital twin platform for federal buildings and Tsinghua University's BIMNet dataset for going from point cloud to BIM.

column2: Singapore: CORENET X becomes mandatory for large projects
column3: From today, building submissions for new projects above 30,000 m² must go through CORENET X, the single permitting platform; BIM models must be delivered in the open IFC+SG format.

column2: UNI 11337-8: the BIM management system becomes a standard
column3: Part 8 of UNI 11337, on the management and governance system for digitalised processes (SGBIM), is open for public enquiry until 17 November: it continues UNI/PdR 74 of 2019 and shifts the focus from individual competences to the organisation as a whole.
